ev.q: analyzed 2009 data from a newly instituted survey, the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS)
Males in Bangladesh were twice as likely as females to notice cigarette advertising (68.0% versus 29.3%)
Overall smoking prevalence among females (1.5%) was far lower than males (44.7%)
In Uruguay, 19.8% of females were current smokers, compared with 30.7% of males
Regardless of age group or region type (urban or rural), males were more likely to smoke than females in all three countries.
In all three countries, awareness of cigarette advertising was greater among females aged 15--24 years than women aged ≥25 years.
is a new nationally representative household survey of persons aged ≥15 years

methods_quotes.q: Statistical significance of differences in values was determined using a chi-square test, with significance determined at p<0.05.
All estimates were weighted to reflect the noninstitutionalized population aged ≥15 years in each country, accounting for clustered sampling in the variance estimation.
† Significant difference between females and males (p<0.05, chi-square test).
¶ Significant difference between younger and older age group (p<0.05, chi-square test).
